title: Path Sum II
statement:
You are given a binary tree whose nodes hold integer values, and an integer `target`. A **root-to-leaf path** starts at the root and ends at a leaf (a node with no children). Find every root-to-leaf path whose node values add up to exactly `target`.

A node with only one child is not a leaf, so a path may not stop there.

The tree is given in **level order**: the first token is the root, then the children of each existing node are listed left then right, from the first node of the level to the last. A missing child is written as `null`, and a missing node has no children listed (they are not represented at all). Trailing `null` tokens are omitted.

Report the matching paths in the order a left-to-right walk of the tree reaches their leaves (visit the left subtree before the right subtree). Each path is written as its node values from the root down to the leaf.

**Follow-up:** in an interview you may be asked to define the tree node class yourself and to return the paths rather than print them. Practise both, and also the iterative version, since the tree can be deep.
inputFormat:
The first line contains the tree in level order: space-separated tokens, each an integer or `null`.
The second line contains the integer `target`.
outputFormat: The first line contains `k`, the number of matching paths. Each of the next `k` lines contains one path: its values from root to leaf, separated by single spaces. If `k` is 0, print only `0`.
constraints: The tree can be as deep as the number of nodes.

examples.explanation: The root 7 has children 3 and 5. Node 3 has leaves 4 and 1; node 5 has a left child 2 and no right child. Leaf paths are 7+3+4=14, 7+3+1=11 and 7+5+2=14, so two paths match, listed left to right.
The root has one child, so it is not a leaf. The only root-to-leaf path is 1, 2 with sum 3, which is not 1.
A single node is both the root and a leaf, and its value equals the target.

complexity.time: O(n * h) in the worst case (O(n) to walk the tree plus the cost of printing the paths)

hints: Walk the tree depth first and keep the current path and its running sum.
Only test the sum at leaves. Remember that a node with exactly one child is not a leaf.
On the way back up undo the last step of the path (backtracking). For deep trees do the walk with an explicit stack, for example by storing parent links for the path instead of copying it.
